research_scope: Five complete source-free reviews of convex combinations, convex hull and product topology; no new meanings, aliases or sources.

amendments.review_rationale: Examined the complete real convexity, convex hull, or indexed product topology formulation with its existing full adjacency, distinguishing set operations from predicates being defined.

references.context: Real vector space: a two-point convex combination tx+(1−t)y, coefficients t and 1−t nonnegative and summing to one.
references.reason: Convex combination is a reusable affine algebra construction.
references.matching_note: Do not conflate with arbitrary affine or linear combination.

references.context: Real analysis: the closed unit interval [0,1]⊆ℝ, including both endpoints, containing permissible convex-combination parameters.
references.reason: The real closed unit interval is an independently reusable set.
references.matching_note: Compare general real interval candidate with endpoint conventions.

references.disposition: Convexity refers to containment of line segments, not topological closure.

references.context: Real vector space: weighted Minkowski set sum tC+(1−t)C={tx+(1−t)y:x,y∈C}, with the two elements selected independently.
references.reason: Weighted Minkowski set arithmetic is a reusable set construction.
references.matching_note: Distinguish pointwise convex combination and scalar multiplication of a set.

references.disposition: This set-inclusion clause for each t∈[0,1] is the defining alternative predicate of convexity, not a separate notion of convexity.
Definition does not assert closure under arbitrary real scalar multiples.

references.phrase: finite convex combination with strictly positive coefficients
references.context: Real affine geometry: finite sum ∑_{j=1}^m λ_j u_j with m≥1, λ_j>0 and ∑ λ_j=1; zero weights can be omitted.
references.reason: Finite convex combination is reusable independently of the convex hull.
references.matching_note: Positive-weight convention equivalent to allowing zeros and dropping zero terms.

references.disposition: The convention conv(∅)=∅ is the boundary case of the convex hull currently being defined, not a self-referential prerequisite.

references.phrase: strict positivity not a restriction on convex hull
references.disposition: Zero-weight terms can be omitted from a finite convex combination.

references.disposition: The family of all convex supersets containing U is specified in the defining construction for conv(U), not an independent special object.

references.context: Set theory: arbitrary intersection of a family of subsets of V, here specialized to the family of convex supersets of U; its specialization equals the convex hull.
references.reason: Arbitrary set intersection is a reusable operation.
references.matching_note: Global audit compare arbitrary-intersection and closure-family references.

references.phrase: convex hull is least convex superset
references.disposition: Intersection definition uses all convex supersets, not one arbitrary convex superset.

references.phrase: basic product of open coordinate sets
references.context: General topology: restricted Cartesian product ∏_{i∈I}U_i where each U_i is open in X_i and U_i=X_i except for finitely many i.
references.reason: Basic product sets are independently reusable before stating the product topology basis.
references.matching_note: Finite-support requirement distinguishes product from box topology.

references.disposition: Restricting only finitely many coordinates in a basic product open is the defining basis condition distinguishing the product topology from the box topology.
No allowance for infinitely many simultaneous proper-coordinate restrictions as basic opens.
